instructions:
skep is a substrate of documents, immutable content, and first-class links, served by the skepd daemon. Each tool here is one wire operation (plus session_info, adapter apparatus); the result text is skepd's response document, verbatim JSON.

Encodings. Tumblers and addresses are dotted-decimal strings ("1.0.1.0.1.0.1.1"), zeros explicit. Unbounded naturals (widths, V-position components) are decimal strings ("5"); non-negative integers are accepted. Log positions (at/as_of), slots, window sizes, and principal ids are plain JSON numbers. Spans are {"start": <tumbler>, "width": <tumbler>}, half-open in the tumbler order; zero-width is invalid; the depth-2 content V-span {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"} names subspace 1 (content), ordinal 1, five positions. V-positions are {"subspace", "ordinal"} naturals; subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

Content granularity is said, never fallen into. In insert's values array, a bare string mints one single-byte value per UTF-8 byte ("hello" is five values at five positions) and {"hex"} one per raw byte; {"atom"}/{"atom_hex"} mint ONE composite value at ONE position whose interior is permanently unaddressable — no link, transclusion, or compare can ever reach inside it, in any document, for the value's whole lifetime. Deliveries are injective: a maximal run of single-byte values renders as one {"content"} item ({"hex"} when the run is not UTF-8), each composite value as its own {"atom"}/{"atom_hex"} item, and a link position as {"ref"}. Count positions, not items: {"content": "hello"} spans five positions, {"atom": "hello"} one.

Rejections are data, not errors. A failed operation answers {"resp": "rejected", "op", "code", "disposition", ...} as a normal tool result; isError marks only failure to reach the daemon. disposition is advisory: permanent (reissuing the same request cannot succeed), reorder (a future committed state may satisfy the precondition; reissue after it commits), retry (transient; the operation did nothing), halt (writes stopped; reads still work). Every write acknowledgment carries at (the commit that made it true); every read carries as_of (its snapshot).

Sessions are this adapter's job: it binds its configured principal automatically and reopens the session after a daemon restart; tokens never surface here. A principal must be delegated an account before the stores accept its writes; session_info reports your principal, your account address (null until delegated), and daemon health. One naming note: in make_link and emit, the schema argument from_ is the wire's from.

tools.name: create_new_document
tools.description: Mint a fresh empty document in account (your own account: resolve it via principal_prefix or session_info). Response: ack_addr with the document's address.

account.description: Account address the document is minted in.

tools.name: delegate
tools.description: Carve new_prefix off your account (or node) and register principal new_id as its owner, atomically. Obtain new_prefix from next_account_prefix; only the owner of the parent may delegate under it. Response: ack_addr with the minted account address.

new_prefix.description: The delegable prefix tumbler, as answered by next_account_prefix.

new_id.description: The principal id registered as the new account's owner.

tools.name: register_node
tools.description: Admit a provisioned node address (bootstrap provisioning; the address is supplied, not minted). Response: ack_addr.

addr.description: The provisioned node address (a raw tumbler).

tools.name: fork
tools.description: Mint a fresh EMPTY account-tier document in your own account. Shares no content: the content-sharing fork is version. Response: ack_addr.

tools.name: next_account_prefix
tools.description: The next delegable prefix under parent (what delegate demands). Response: maybe_addr; addr null means an ineligible parent.

tools.name: principal_prefix
tools.description: Any principal's account address (public, immutable registry data). Response: maybe_addr; addr null means an unknown principal.

tools.name: insert
tools.description: Insert content into doc at V-position at; each element of values is one write form. A bare string mints one single-byte value per UTF-8 byte (per-byte text, the substrate's text discipline); {"hex"} one per raw byte; {"atom"}/{"atom_hex"} mint ONE composite value at one position whose interior is permanently unaddressable. Mixed arrays concatenate in order; an insert totalling zero values is rejected empty_content. Response: ack_addr with the first minted I-address.

at.description: Insertion V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

values.description: Write forms, concatenated in order. "" and {"hex": ""} are vacuous; a zero-byte atom is not expressible.

oneOf.description: Per-byte text: one single-byte value per UTF-8 byte.
Per-byte raw bytes: one single-byte value per byte.
ONE composite value of the string's UTF-8 bytes, at one position; its interior is permanently unaddressable.
ONE composite value of the raw bytes, at one position; interior permanently unaddressable.

tools.name: delete
tools.description: Remove width positions of doc starting at p. Response: ack.

p.description: First removed V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

width.description: Number of positions, an unbounded natural: decimal string canonically ("2"); a non-negative integer is accepted.

tools.name: copy
tools.description: Transclude the given source spans into doc at at — shared identity, not copied bytes. Response: ack.

at.description: Destination V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

specs.description: V-specs naming the transcluded source spans.

items.description: V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

span.description: Half-open V-span: depth-2 content example {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"} = subspace 1, ordinal 1, five positions; zero-width is invalid.

tools.name: rearrange
tools.description: Pivot/swap doc's content about the cut positions. Response: ack.

items.description: V-position: subspace 1 = content, 2 = links; ordinals 1-based.

tools.name: version
tools.description: The content-sharing, copy-on-write fork of d_src. Response: ack_addr with the new version's address.

tools.name: make_link
tools.description: Create an open content link homed in home; from_ (the wire's from — renamed in this schema only, mapped back by the adapter), to, and ty are V-spec sets resolved against current arrangements (the recorded endsets are permanent I-spans). The type slot must resolve nonempty. Response: ack_addr with the link's address.

from_.description: FROM endset as V-specs (the wire argument named from).

items.description: V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

span.description: Half-open V-span: depth-2 content example {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"}; zero-width is invalid.

items.description: V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

span.description: Half-open V-span: depth-2 content example {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"}; zero-width is invalid.

ty.description: TYPE endset as V-specs; must resolve nonempty.

items.description: V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

span.description: Half-open V-span: depth-2 content example {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"}; zero-width is invalid.

tools.name: emit
tools.description: Gated typed-relation emission: a managed tuple of type ty (the type key as an endset, usually unit subtree spans of type addresses) from from_ (the wire's from — renamed in this schema only, mapped back by the adapter) to the to addresses, homed in home. Idempotent within a type class: re-emitting an existing tuple acks the incumbent address. Response: ack_addr.

ty.description: The type key as an endset: I-spans, usually unit subtree spans of type addresses.

items.description: Half-open I-span over permanent addresses; zero-width is invalid.

from_.description: Tuple source address (the wire argument named from).

items.description: Target address.

tools.name: nullify
tools.description: The sole retraction path: retract target (a link) from the active view, by a retraction homed in home. Response: ack_addr with the retraction's address.

home.description: Home document address of the retraction.

tools.name: assert_sup
tools.description: Record that old is superseded by new. Response: ack_addr with the claim's address.

home.description: Home document address of the claim.

tools.name: edit_link
tools.description: One composite: create a successor of link original (endsets given as content V-specs; the type slot either {"addrs": [...]} or {"resolve": [...]}), homed in d_s, plus the supersession claim homed in d_a. Response: ack_edit with the successor link and its supersession claim.

successor.description: The successor's endsets. Nested keys are wire shape verbatim (this from is not renamed).

items.description: V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

span.description: Half-open V-span: depth-2 content example {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"}; zero-width is invalid.

items.description: V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

span.description: Half-open V-span: depth-2 content example {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"}; zero-width is invalid.

ty.description: The type slot: exactly one of {"addrs": [addresses]} (address-denoting) or {"resolve": [V-specs]} (content-resolved).

items.description: Type address.
V-spec: a span of some document's arrangement.

d_s.description: Home document of the successor link.

d_a.description: Home document of the supersession claim.

tools.name: read_link
tools.description: The link value at a, verbatim: {"slots": [endset, ...]}, positional, 1-based (slot 1 = FROM, 2 = TO, 3 = TYPE). Response: link_value; link null means no link resides at that address.

tools.name: follow_link
tools.description: The coverage of slot slot of link a. Response: follow — {"ok": [spans]} (possibly empty) versus {"err": "invalid"} are different defined answers: empty endset is not the same as no such link/slot.

tools.name: retrieve_v
tools.description: Deliver the content of the given (doc, span) specs, in submitted order. Response: delivery — items with granularity intact: per-byte runs as one {"content"}/{"hex"} item, each composite value its own {"atom"}/{"atom_hex"} item, link positions as {"ref"}.

items.description: One (doc, span) spec.

span.description: Half-open V-span: depth-2 content example {"start": "1.1", "width": "0.5"} = five positions; zero-width is invalid.

tools.name: retrieve_doc_v_span
tools.description: The single V-span covering doc's arrangement. Response: span_set.

tools.name: retrieve_doc_v_span_set
tools.description: doc's exact per-subspace extents: one span per occupied subspace ([S,1] with width = that subspace's position count; content before links), empty for a registered-empty document. Response: span_set.

tools.name: show_origin
tools.description: The origin documents of the positions in span of doc. Response: addrs.

span.description: Half-open V-span of doc's arrangement; zero-width is invalid.

tools.name: show_deletions
tools.description: The deletions between two versions, both directions: each half of the report is the set of I-addresses deleted from one document yet current in the other. Response: deletions.

tools.name: compare
tools.description: The shared-content correspondence between two region sets. Response: compare — pairs, each naming a shared run of width positions at u1 in d1 and u2 in d2.

items.description: Region: a document and spans of its arrangement.
Half-open V-span; zero-width is invalid.
